findings.summary: Dead pager rule targets non-arrow buttons that the pager does not render.
findings.consequence: Future pager styling fixes can be made against this scoped selector without affecting the actual non-arrow controls, leaving behavior dependent on the broader global pager link rules instead.
findings.evidence: The owned selector `.littb_pager .ctrl li:not(.arrows) > button` excludes the only pager `<button>` elements, which are inside `li.arrows` at lines 1596-1614. The non-arrow pager controls are `<a role="button">` at lines 1617, 1620, and 1626, so this selector and its disabled companion do not match the current page DOM.
findings.recommendation: Delete the non-arrow pager button selector block and its disabled companion, or convert the non-arrow template controls to real buttons and keep one matching selector.
verification: Inspected current template structure in app/pages/sök.vue around the pager Teleport.
Searched repository usage of `.littb_pager`, `.ctrl`, and pager button/link controls.

findings.summary: Dead navigator button rule targets elements that the author navigator does not render.
findings.consequence: The page carries a duplicate styling branch that has no effect today, so navigator visual behavior is actually governed by the global `.navigator a` and `li a.selected` styles rather than this scoped rule.
findings.evidence: The owned selector `.navigator button` targets buttons, but the navigator template renders `<a role="button">` controls at lines 1651 and 1662. The selected state is applied to those anchors via `:class`, so `.navigator button.selected` also cannot match the current DOM.
findings.recommendation: Delete the `.navigator button` and `.navigator button.selected` blocks, or retarget them to the actual anchor controls if scoped overrides are required.
verification: Inspected current navigator template in app/pages/sök.vue.
Searched repository usage of `.navigator` and reviewed relevant behavior tests for navigator role and selection.
